text:
cs-agent: ACME PROD is seeing a spike of 503s to /v1/generate starting ~2026-02-14 12:05 UTC. Customer reports timeouts and failed toolcalls. Sample req id: req_8d3f7a. Sending logs now, paging oncall.

oncall-ashley: grabbing logs and metrics from hosted-a pool. I see a pattern of runner exits then container respawn. Paging infra.

cs-agent: sample payload (redacted) includes huge context + tool call. Customer says requests were streaming when they observed failures.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1024. Attachments: hosted-a/runner/req_8d3f7a/logs, hosted-a/core-dumps/2345.

oncall-ashley: here's the last lines from the runner log around the crash:
```
[12:04:58] runner[2345]: INFO Start streaming request req_8d3f7a ctx_len=102400
[12:05:02] runner[2345]: WARN kv_prefetch: reserving 1.2GiB
[12:05:03] runner[2345]: ERROR CUDA error at inference.cc:420: out of memory
[12:05:03] runner[2345]: ERROR fatal: attempting to allocate 12884901888 bytes
[12:05:03] runner[2345]: SIGSEGV (signal 11) at 0x7f23a1c3
[12:05:04] systemd: container exited with status 139, restarting
```

dev-raj: that allocation size looks wrong for prefetch (12.8GB). Might be a multiplier bug when streaming with toolcall KVs. Are we doing context->prefetch*shard_count math anywhere?

sara: @dev-raj good call. I recall a recent change to kv prefetch that multiplies by num_shards to warm more of the KV cache. If ctx_len is large we can blow past per-GPU budgets.

martin: can we repro locally with the customer's payload? If so we should get a coredump, run a smaller reproduction with env RUNNER_DEBUG=1 and --disable-kv-prefetch to confirm.

cs-agent: uploaded a sanitized payload to the incident workspace: /incidents/INC-2026-1024/inputs/acme-large-stream.json

oncall-ashley: repro attempt: launched runner with --disable-kv-prefetch and ran the payload. No crash, memory peaks ~10.2GiB and finishes. Re-enable prefetch and it OOMs & segfaults reproducibly.

dev-raj: ok that narrows it. Temporary mitigation: disable kv_prefetch on hosted-a pools for the time being and add a rate-limit for context size > 32k tokens. I'll open a short-lived feature flag.

sara: applying mitigation: toggled kv_prefetch=false on pool hosted-a at 12:35 UTC and set request_size_limit=32768 for streaming routes. Will monitor.

infra-bot: Policy change applied: hosted-a kv_prefetch=false (actor=sara).

oncall-ashley: immediate impact: 503 rate for acme-prod down from 11.7% -> 0.9% within 5m. Latency improved. :thumbsup:

martin: follow-ups (action items):
- dev-raj: root cause triage and fix kv-prefetch multiplier logic (PR + unit tests)
- eng-ml: add regression test with large streaming+toolcall workload to model harness
- oncall: capture minidumps for next crash (if any) and enable extra coredump retention for 24h
- cs-agent: notify ACME that we've applied a mitigation and are working on a fix; offer guidance to reduce context size as a workaround

dev-raj: starting a bisect of kv_prefetch changes, will target a fix and hotpatch within 48h. PR link when ready: https://git.internal/redwood/runner/pulls/ (will fill)

cs-agent: CS notified ACME at 12:40 UTC, they confirmed reduced 503s. They want ETA for permanent fix and postmortem.

sara: leaving this thread open. Will promote the fix to canary pool first, then roll to hosted if green.

martin: assigning postmortem owner: @dev-raj. Please include timeline and customer impact metrics in the postmortem.

oncall-ashley: logging done to INC-2026-1024; tagging ops-runbook and billing-impact.

cs-agent: closing customer escalation (temp) — will update when PR merged and patch released. Thanks everyone.
